what: Aptiv makes the electrical architecture of a car: the wiring harnesses, connectors, computers and software that carry power and data between everything in the vehicle.
customers: Carmakers worldwide, who design its architecture into vehicle platforms years before production.
money: wiring harnesses, connectors and power distribution
driver assistance systems, cockpit computing and software
moat: The electrical architecture is designed with the vehicle itself, so once Aptiv wins a platform it supplies it for the model's whole life, typically five to seven years.
risks: A 0.8% net margin: wiring harnesses are labour-intensive and heavily price-negotiated
Vehicle production volumes have been flat and carmakers demand annual price cuts
opportunities: Analysts see about 52% upside, with 18 covering the stock
Electric and software-defined vehicles need far more electrical content per car, which is exactly what Aptiv sells
watch: Growth relative to vehicle production, and the planned separation of the electrical business.
